newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels accuse army of peasant massacre.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels accuse army of peasant massacre.

text.p: Leftist rebels charged on Friday that the massacre of more than 30 peasants in eastern Colombia almost two weeks ago was carried out by army troops disguised as right-wing paramilitary fighters.
At the time, the security forces blamed the attack, in the town of Mapiripan in Meta Province, on the so-called Guaviare Front, a previously unknown paramilitary gang.
Gen. Agustin Ardila, head of the army's Fourth Division which operates in Meta province, rejected the rebels' accusation, made in a communique.

The charge came on the same day the United States agreed to unfreeze about $85 million in military aid to the Colombian army that had been blocked until President Ernesto Samper's administration pledged not to distribute the weaponry to anti-guerrilla battalions of the army.

"A counterinsurgency patrol of 150 men ... passing themselves off as paramilitaries captured several peasants and went into Mapiripan," the Eastern Bloc of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's oldest and largest guerrilla force, said in its statement, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
"They spent four days there until they were joined by two other patrols and on July 21 with guns, machetes and chain-saws massacred 35 defenceless peasants," the rebels said.
They said the troops headed back to their bases in neighbouring Guaviare Province after the killings.

"I can say that there were no members of the public security forces involved in the massacre. ... We have fulfilled all orders from the head of the armed forces, which includes full respect for human rights," Ardila told Reuters.

At the time of the massacre, witnesses spoke of at least 30 deaths, but so far only five bodies, some decapitated, have been recovered. The Communist Party said some of the dead and missing were members of its organisation.
An official of the International Committee of the Red Cross said at the time the true number of victims might never be known, since many corpses were thought to have been thrown into a nearby river.
